bookCredit: Prince Caspian by C. S. Lewis (1951) is quoted only in short lines.
title: Into Trufflehunter’s Cave

banner.alt: A storm over black mountains and a dark pine forest, with one warm firelit cave mouth low in the hills

keepsake.name: golden apple
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. From the orchard the moles planted, grown wild up to the walls.

postcard.h: What a prince carries at midnight
body: The Doctor wakes Caspian, packs a wallet with cold chicken, bread, an apple and a flask, then hands him a purse of gold and a horn.
Then a storm, a bolting horse, and three faces by a cave fire.
postcard.word: A usurper takes a throne that is not theirs. The word fits Miraz.

mission.h: Build the start and end of Caspian’s night
mission.p: One side: what he carried from the castle. Other side: Trufflehunter’s firelit cave.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. the start: the wallet, the chicken, the flask, the purse of gold
  2. between: Destrier, running through the pines
  3. the end: the fire in the cave, the Badger beside it
steps.say: Stand by the cave fire, where Caspian woke. Practice these 2 sentences:
steps.frame: “___ does / does not trust Caspian. I know because ___.”
steps.extra: Put a Wooden Mug by the fire: the sweet, hot drink Trufflehunter gives him.
steps.fits: the wallet, the horse and the cave

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the wallet and purse, Destrier, and the fire with the Badger, and you say 2 sentences: one of the three in the cave, whether they trust Caspian, and a detail from Chapter 5.

alt.p: Six characters from Chapter 5. Match each one to what the chapter tells you about them.
alt.gameH: Tap a name, then tap what the chapter says

pairs.b: wakes Caspian at night and gives him two gifts
pairs.why: A little purse of gold, and something far better: Queen Susan’s horn.

pairs.b: called himself Lord Protector before he called himself King
pairs.why: He weeded out the great lords one by one, the Doctor says.

pairs.b: saddled and waiting at the corner of the orchard
pairs.why: He bolts in the storm when thunder cracks overhead.

pairs.b: the oldest and kindest of the three, a Badger
pairs.why: He gives Caspian a drink and says beasts do not change; they hold on.

pairs.b: the Black Dwarf who wants to be rid of the Human
pairs.why: He jumps up with a hand on his dagger when Caspian says Miraz is his uncle.

pairs.b: the Red Dwarf who says it is not the creature’s fault
pairs.why: Bulbs and bolsters! He and the Badger hold Nikabrik back.

alt.miss: Not that one. Think about who was in the castle and who was in the cave.

write.q: Pick one of the three in the cave: Trufflehunter, Nikabrik or Trumpkin. In 2 sentences, say whether they trust Caspian and give one thing they do in Chapter 5 that shows it.

scripts.brief: Hello, dear. It’s Nell. In Chapter 5 the Doctor wakes Caspian in the night and packs a wallet with cold chicken, bread, an apple and a flask. Then come a purse of gold, a horn, a storm, a bolting horse, and a cave with three faces by the fire. Build where the night began and where it ended, and tell me which of the three trusted the boy.
scripts.alt: No headset? Sit by my bench. Chapter 5 is crowded with new names: a tutor, a usurper, a horse, a badger and two dwarfs. Match each one to what the chapter tells you, and the cave will feel like a room you know.
scripts.saved: Both ends of the night are built, and the fire is lit in the cave. Here is your golden apple. Keep it, and remember that a badger holds on when dwarfs and men forget.

testPara: Nikabrik does not trust Caspian. I know because in Chapter 5 he jumps up with his hand on his dagger when he hears Miraz is Caspian's uncle.
